description: A guide to the best beaches on Odisha's Bay of Bengal coast: Puri's Blue Flag Golden Beach and sand art, Chandrabhaga and Ramchandi near Konark, Gopalpur and Sunapur in Ganjam, Chandipur where the sea recedes at low tide, Talasari near the Bengal border, and the olive ridley nesting coast, with cyclone season and swimming advice.
dek: Odisha's beaches sit beside some of India's great temples and one of the world's largest turtle nesting sites. Here is how they compare.

intro: Odisha's coastline runs for about 480 km along the Bay of Bengal, from the West Bengal border to Andhra Pradesh. Its beaches are wide, flat and sandy, and many are tied to pilgrimage: Puri with the Jagannath Temple and Konark with the Sun Temple, both part of the popular Golden Triangle of Odisha with Bhubaneswar.

The coast is also a major nesting ground for olive ridley sea turtles, and Chilika, Asia's largest brackish-water lagoon, lies just inland. The best time to visit is October to February; the coast is exposed to cyclones, especially in October and November and before the monsoon.
quickAnswer: The best beaches in Odisha are Puri's Golden Beach, which holds Blue Flag certification, Chandrabhaga and Ramchandi near Konark, Gopalpur and the Blue Flag Sunapur beach in Ganjam, Chandipur, where the sea recedes several kilometres at low tide, and quiet Talasari near the Bengal border. Visit from October to February and check cyclone warnings. At Puri, bathe only in guarded zones.
takeaways: Puri's Golden Beach has Blue Flag certification and traditional lifeguards (nuliyas) in the bathing zone.
Chandrabhaga is about 3 km from the Konark Sun Temple.
Chandipur is known for the sea retreating several kilometres at low tide.
Rushikulya and Gahirmatha are among the world's largest olive ridley nesting sites.
October to February is best; watch for cyclone warnings in October and November.

items.name: Puri
body: Puri's beach runs in front of the town, a short walk from the Jagannath Temple. The certified Golden Beach stretch has managed facilities and lifeguards, and Puri is also home to sand artist Sudarsan Pattnaik, whose work appears on the beach. Nuliyas, the traditional lifeguards in conical hats, help bathers in the guarded zone. The International Sand Art Festival is held on Chandrabhaga beach in December in some years.

items.name: Chandrabhaga
body: About 3 km from the Konark Sun Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, Chandrabhaga is known for sunrise and for festivals held on the sand.

items.name: Ramchandi
body: Where the Kushabhadra river meets the sea between Puri and Konark, a quieter beach with a small temple.

facts.Best for: A stop on the marine drive

items.name: Gopalpur
body: A small, former colonial port town with a calm atmosphere, a lighthouse and a long beach, about three hours south of Bhubaneswar.

items.name: Sunapur
body: A Blue Flag-certified beach in Ganjam district with lifeguard towers and managed facilities.

items.name: Rushikulya
body: The Rushikulya river mouth is one of the world's largest olive ridley mass-nesting sites, usually in February and March, with hatchlings emerging weeks later. Access to nesting areas is controlled by the forest department.

items.name: Chandipur
body: Near Balasore, the sea at Chandipur retreats several kilometres at low tide, leaving wide wet flats you can walk on, then returns with the tide. Check tide times before walking out.

items.name: Talasari
body: A quiet beach near the West Bengal border, with red crabs, casuarinas and an estuary; easy to combine with Digha.

items.name: Chilika Lake
body: Asia's largest brackish-water lagoon, south of Puri, with Irrawaddy dolphins near Satapada and migratory birds in winter.

items.name: Bhitarkanika
body: Mangroves and saltwater crocodiles in a national park near the Gahirmatha turtle coast.

sections.heading: How many days?
paras: Three days covers Puri, Konark and Chilika. Add two days for Gopalpur, and another for Chandipur in the north.

safety: Swim only at beaches with lifeguards, inside the flagged zone, and never when a red flag is up or during the monsoon.
At Puri, bathe only in the guarded zone and follow the nuliyas' instructions; currents are strong.
Check cyclone warnings, especially in October, November and May.
At Chandipur, check tide times and walk back well before the tide turns.
Keep away from turtle nesting areas unless with forest department staff.

faqs.q: Which is the best beach in Odisha?
faqs.a: Puri's Golden Beach is the best known; Chandrabhaga near Konark and Gopalpur are quieter alternatives.

faqs.q: Which Odisha beaches have Blue Flag certification?
faqs.a: Puri's Golden Beach and Sunapur in Ganjam district.

faqs.q: What is special about Chandipur beach?
faqs.a: The sea retreats several kilometres at low tide, leaving flats you can walk on.

faqs.q: When can I see turtle nesting in Odisha?
faqs.a: Mass nesting at Rushikulya usually happens in February and March, with hatchlings weeks later. Access is controlled.

faqs.q: Is it safe to swim at Puri?
faqs.a: Only in the guarded bathing zone, in calm conditions, following the lifeguards.
